questions: What type of chiropractic do you do?
faqs.answer: McTimoney chiropractors focus on the spine and the neuro-musculoskeletal system and how conditions affecting these areas can affect your health and performance.

questions: Do I need a referral from my doctor?
Do I need to see my GP first?
faqs.answer: You do not need a referral from your doctor to see a chiropractor. With your permission the clinic will let your GP know you are receiving chiropractic treatment and, where needed, refer you back for further investigation.

questions: How long does the first appointment take?
faqs.answer: The initial consultation takes around 45 minutes. All follow-on treatments are 30 minutes long.

questions: Is it safe for people of all ages?
Do you treat children or older people?
faqs.answer: Yes. The clinic says the gentle treatment is suitable for all ages, from the young through to the elderly.
Yes. All chiropractors are governed by the General Chiropractic Council and each must have a registration number to practise.

questions: Will I need to get undressed?
faqs.answer: For the first visit you need to undress down to your underwear because of the neurological tests; if you are uncomfortable with that you may wear shorts and a strappy top or vest. For follow-up treatments, tracksuit bottoms and a t-shirt are fine.

The McTimoney adjustments are light and gentle and rarely painful. After treatment you may notice a brief period of stiffness or tiredness, but more often patients report a feeling of wellbeing and relief from stress and pain.

The clinic says chiropractic treatment is very safe. A full medical history is taken before any treatment, and if the chiropractor suspects a problem needing further investigation you will be referred to your GP first.

questions: How many treatments will I need?
How many sessions do people need?
faqs.answer: Most people need between two and six treatments, initially weekly and then spaced out as the condition improves. It depends on your age, the nature of the problem and how long you have had it.

questions: Will I get advice so the problem does not come back?
faqs.answer: Yes. You will get postural advice after treatment and may be given some basic exercises or stretches if the chiropractor thinks they would help.

You can book online or by calling 0118 375 0803; the clinic says you can also book through Facebook. If there is no suitable appointment, check the online booking for cancellations or call to be put on a waiting list.
The clinic is at 22 London Road, Twyford, Reading, RG10 9ER.
